provenance.instrument: Borough of Downingtown Zoning Ordinance of 1989 (Chapter 287 Zoning, Ord. No. 89-14 of 10-11-1989, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 DO0156, Borough of Downingtown. The definitions name the East Lancaster Avenue National Register district and Chester County records, and the zoning hearing notice goes to the Chester County Planning Commission (287-7, 287-142B), so this is Downingtown borough, Chester County. District use lists and area and bulk rules are text in Articles V to XV. The attachments are a planting table and sign appendices. The Floodplain District is governed by Chapter 150, which 287-12 incorporates. New Laws: none (0)
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 table of contents: 'Includes legislation through 07-01-2026.' New Laws (0). 287-76 and 150-6.02 carry Ord. No. 2026-03 of 7-1-2026
checks: The code has no accessory dwelling unit use. The words searched (accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, garage apartment, second dwelling, ECHO, extended family, elder cottage, tenant house, temporary dwelling, living quarters, caretaker, conversion) find only the conversion of dwellings (287-94), the conversion and group home definitions and other uses. No residential district lists an ADU (287-19, 287-23, 287-27, 287-32)

Each district lists its principal uses 'and no other', and permits as accessory uses only 'Uses customarily accessory and incidental to' residential uses, home occupations and pools (287-19B, 287-23B, 287-27B, 287-32B). A dwelling unit is for 'occupancy by only one family' with no enclosed space in common with another unit except halls and porches (287-7). There is no general rule for uses not provided for. Only some nonresidential districts let the Zoning Hearing Board approve a use of the same general character as their listed uses, such as C-1 (287-37C(4)), and none of R-1 to R-4 does

Conversion of dwellings: a single-family detached dwelling in R-3, R-4 or C-1 that existed on the chapter's effective date (10-11-1989) may become two units by special exception, only in a building with at least 3,000 sq ft of floor area on that date. Two parking spaces per unit, the two-family area and bulk rules of the district, no outside change except for safety, and each new unit at least 500 sq ft. A unit above the ground floor needs plans approved by the Department of Labor and Industry, and the lot keeps the district's building, impervious and vegetative coverage limits (287-94B, 287-27C(6), 287-32C(7), 287-37C(3))

Two-family dwellings (twin or duplex) are permitted by right in R-3 and R-4: 5,000 sq ft per family in R-3 and 4,000 sq ft per family in R-4, 70 ft wide for a duplex (287-28B, 287-33B). That is a building for two units. Turning the existing house into two units is a conversion

R-1 permits by right the single-family detached dwelling and agriculture under 287-95. R-2 permits only the single-family detached dwelling (287-19A, 287-23A). On a property of five acres or more used for agriculture that has a primary residence, one more single-family detached dwelling may stand, unless a second dwelling was already there on the chapter's effective date (287-95A, G)

Accessory buildings: 3 ft from side and rear lot lines and 5 ft from the edge of any alley or street at the side or rear (287-20I, 287-24I, 287-28E, 287-33F). A private garage may be at most 15 ft tall (287-74). Garden sheds and similar uninhabitable structures at most 12 ft (287-73E)

Lot coverage is split: a maximum building coverage and a separate 'Maximum other impervious surface coverage' for paving (287-20, 287-24, 287-28, 287-33). Lot area excludes rights-of-way and, where they make up more than 20% of the lot, floodplain, slopes over 20%, high water table soils and wetlands (287-7 'Lot area')

Parking: 'Single-family, two-family, quadraplex and townhouse dwellings: two parking spaces for each dwelling unit'. A fraction of one-half space or less is disregarded (287-107A, D(1)(a)). Parking areas may cover no more than 50% of any required yard (287-103C)

Floodplain District (Chapter 150 through 287-12): 'Within any identified floodplain area, any new construction, except storage sheds, decks, and fences constructed in compliance with Subsection E, F, and G below, shall be prohibited', unless a variance is granted under Article IX (150-6.02, Ord. No. 2026-03). New construction is a structure begun on or after September 29, 2017, with its later improvements (150-10.02). An addition to an older house is an improvement: no expansion may raise the base flood elevation, work of 50% or more of market value is a substantial improvement, and in the floodway, or within 50 ft landward of the top of bank where no floodway is mapped, it needs a DEP permit (150-8.01, 8.02). An accessory structure in the floodplain may not be designed or used for human habitation and may have no sanitary facilities (150-6.02E)

Floodplain variances (Zoning Hearing Board, 150-9.01): 'No variance shall be granted within any identified floodplain area that would cause any increase in BFE', none in the floodway or in an AE area without floodway that raises it, and none for the prohibited activities of Article VII (150-9.02A(1), (2), (3), (5))

Steep Slope Conservation District (slopes of 20% or more): a single-family detached dwelling only by special exception, and impervious cover in the district at most half the base district maximum (287-13E(3), (4)). No structure on soils with a seasonally high water table within one foot of the surface (287-14A). Wetlands need a delineation and any required permits (287-14B)

Nonconforming lots: a vacant lot of record may be built on if the yards are met, else by special exception, but not if it is under half the required area or width (287-125A). A nonconforming structure may be extended by up to 25% of its floor area on the effective date if the extension meets the area and bulk rules (287-124C)

Historic Resources Overlay (287-101.3): 'All changes to buildings and structures within the Historic Resources Overlay District shall be reviewed and approved by Borough Council' (F). Additions are subordinate in massing, height, size and scale, and 'The size of the addition, when viewed from existing streets, shall not exceed the size of the existing historic building' (D(1)). New garages and outbuildings follow historic building groupings, and existing window and door openings are not enlarged (D(8), (9)). Overlays not read in full: Central Business Revitalization (design standards of SALDO 256-56.1), Adaptive Reuse/Mixed-Use, Mixed-Use, Traditional Neighborhood Development, Uptown Transportation Development, Kardon Park Redevelopment and Woodbine

Lodgers: a residential accessory use is 'The renting of rooms within the dwelling in which the lessor resides, or in a building accessory thereto, to not more than two nontransient persons, with or without the provision of table board for such persons. One additional off-street parking space shall be provided for each such occupant' (287-91B(5)). This is by right in every residential district. It is not a dwelling unit, so the rooms have no kitchen of their own

C-1 permits no house by right, so a house there is a nonconforming use. A dwelling unit may be part of a building whose ground floor or front holds a permitted commercial use, by special exception (287-37C(2), 287-38K). C-1 rules for all uses: lot 2,500 sq ft, no front, side or rear yard except one 15 ft side yard without rear access, building coverage 50%, other impervious 30%, vegetative area at least 10% (287-38)

Steep Slope Conservation District: the only uses by right there are parks and outdoor recreation, grading for the least part of a driveway to a house, emergency access roads and their accessory uses (287-13E(2)). A single-family detached dwelling, roads, sealed wells and sewers are special exceptions (287-13E(3)). A two-family dwelling, an addition or an accessory building for a second unit is not among them on the steep slope area
Variances: Zoning Hearing Board on the findings of MPC 910.2 (287-144A). No bar on a use variance was found

status.note: No residential district lists a second unit on a house lot. R-3 and R-4 permit two-family dwellings by right, R-3, R-4 and C-1 permit the conversion of a large older house into two units by special exception (287-94), and R-1 allows a second house on a farm of five acres or more (287-95G)

path.note: A second unit on a house lot is not a listed use, and each district lists its uses 'and no other', so the path is a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board (MPC 910.2). R-3 and R-4 permit two-family dwellings by right, and a large older house may be converted into two units by special exception (see the other paths)

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board on the findings of MPC 910.2. No bar on a use variance

value.name: Conversion of a single-family detached dwelling (R-3, R-4, C-1)
value.conditions: A single-family detached dwelling that existed on 10-11-1989 converted into two units, each with its own kitchen, bath and sleeping space. The building had at least 3,000 sq ft of floor area on that date. Two parking spaces per unit with direct access to a street or alley. The two-family area and bulk rules of the district apply (5,000 sq ft per family in R-3, 4,000 sq ft per family in R-4, 70 ft wide for a duplex). No outside change except for safety, and fire escapes at the rear where practicable. Each new unit at least 500 sq ft. A unit above the ground floor needs plans approved by the Department of Labor and Industry. The lot keeps the district's building, impervious and vegetative coverage limits

requires.condition: An existing single-family detached dwelling to convert
The house existed on the chapter's effective date. The chapter was adopted 10-11-1989, which is used here
At least 3,000 sq ft of floor area on the effective date

value.note: The lot figures read the two-family rule of 'Minimum lot area: 5,000 square feet per family' (R-3) and 4,000 (R-4) as 10,000 and 8,000 sq ft. C-1 has no two-family rule, so its rule for all uses applies: 2,500 sq ft (287-38A). A house in C-1 is a nonconforming use, since C-1 permits no house by right

value.name: Two-family dwelling (R-3)
value.conditions: A twin or duplex building for two families. 5,000 sq ft per family, 70 ft wide for a duplex (40 ft per twin unit). Building coverage 35%, other impervious surface 25%. Front 25 ft, side 10 ft with 25 ft for both for a duplex, rear 35 ft, height 35 ft. Two parking spaces per unit

requires.condition: A building for two units. Turning the existing house into two units is a conversion instead

value.note: Read as 5,000 sq ft for each of two families

value.name: Two-family dwelling (R-4)
value.conditions: A twin or duplex building for two families. 4,000 sq ft per family, 70 ft wide for a duplex (40 ft per twin unit). Building coverage 40%, other impervious surface 25%. Front 20 ft, side 8 ft with 20 ft for both for a duplex, rear 25 ft, height 35 ft. Two parking spaces per unit

requires.condition: A building for two units. Turning the existing house into two units is a conversion instead

value.note: Read as 4,000 sq ft for each of two families

value.name: Second single-family detached dwelling on a farm (R-1)
value.conditions: On a property of five acres or more used for agriculture that has a primary residence, one more single-family detached dwelling may stand. Not if a second dwelling already stood on the property on the chapter's effective date. It is sited so that a later subdivision for the tenant house would meet the rules. Two parking spaces per dwelling unit

requires.condition: A primary residence on the property
The property is used for agriculture under 287-95
No second dwelling stood on the property on the chapter's effective date

value.note: Five acres is 217,800 sq ft. Agriculture needs at least five acres (287-95A)

historic_bypass.note: The Historic Resources Overlay (287-101.3) adds Borough Council review and design rules. Adaptive reuse there is a design rule, not a use grant. 287-127 lets the Zoning Hearing Board waive the 25% extension limit for a nonconforming historic structure. No historic path for an ADU

districts_read_no_listing.note: None lists an accessory dwelling unit. R-3 and R-4 list two-family dwellings and conversions of dwellings. C-1 lists conversions and dwelling units with a ground floor commercial use

value.condition: 'Within any identified floodplain area, any new construction, except storage sheds, decks, and fences constructed in compliance with Subsection E, F, and G below, shall be prohibited', unless a variance is granted under Article IX. A variance may not raise the base flood elevation.

An addition to a house begun on or after September 29, 2017 is new construction, which is prohibited in the floodplain unless a variance is granted under Article IX. For an older house the addition is an improvement under 150-8.02.

In the floodplain any construction or development needs a permit. Work on an existing building: no expansion may raise the base flood elevation, work of 50% or more of the building's market value is a substantial improvement, and in the floodway, or within 50 ft landward of the top of bank where no floodway is mapped, a DEP permit is needed. An accessory structure in the floodplain may not be designed or used for human habitation.

In an AE zone without a floodway 'No new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse, unless the appropriate permit is obtained from the Department of Environmental Protection's regional office'.

Steep Slope Conservation District (slopes of 20% or more): on the steep slope area only parks, driveway grading, emergency access roads and their accessory uses are by right, and a single-family detached dwelling only by special exception. An addition, accessory building or two-family dwelling is not permitted there. Impervious cover in the district at most half the base district maximum. A Borough Engineer review of slope, grading and drainage plans comes first.
No structure may be built on soils whose seasonally high water table is within one foot of the surface (Linside silt loam excepted).

Historic Resources Overlay: all changes to buildings and structures need review and approval by Borough Council. An addition is subordinate to the historic building, and its size seen from existing streets may not exceed the building's. New garages and outbuildings follow historic building groupings, and existing window and door openings are not enlarged.
